messages.author: 7960654ffa0b3bcf
messages.subject: gl.filter.hamming removes information from gl@other$loc.metrics (rdepth missing)
parts:
Hi,

I noticed that the gl.filter.hamming command removes information from gl@other$loc.metrics, when I went through the analysis.
I wanted to look at the final read depth of the SNPs that I had retained and compare it to the average read depth at the beginning, but I noticed that it was missing from the loc metrics after the hamming filter step. Basically its replaced with the MAF in the loc metrics.

I assume this information is just dropped then? Is there some way to retain it when using the command?

Thanks,

 Flo


(I originally posted this issue on github, but it seems this forum is the place to be - sorry for crossposting)

Yes my data is from Diversity Array Technolgy, I use the provided 2row format (xx_SNP_2.csv). messages.author: a3ea45e87285d820
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] gl.filter.hamming removes information from gl@other$loc.metrics (rdepth missing)
parts:
Hi Flo,

I still cannot replicate the error:

gl <- gl.recalc.metrics(testset.gl)
names(gl@other$loc.metrics)
gl@other$loc.metrics$rdepth <- 1
names(gl@other$loc.metrics)
gl2 <- gl.filter.hamming(gl, threshold = 0.25)
names(gl@other$loc.metrics)

And read depth is still there. Maybe if you could copy your genlight object to gl, and then do

names(gl@other$loc.metrics)
gl2 <- gl.filter.hamming(gl, threshold = 0.25)
names(gl2@other$loc.metrics)

and see if rdepth is in there before and after the filter?

You cannot recalculate read depth. It needs to be back-calculated at the time of reading in the data using the locus metrics supplied by DArT.

If you do the above and can replicate the problem, I can pin it down.

A

parts:
Hi Arthur,

I followed your suggestion and it worked, which is strange considering that the only difference to my script is that I copied my object to <gl> instead using my variable name which was something like r5.
One more thing, I am not quite sure if I correctly understand the settings for this filter. So e.g: gl2 <- gl.filter.hamming(gl, threshold = 0.25) would filter all SNPs with a hamming distance lower than 4 (i.e. 4 bases difference out of 100 bases is 25 =0.25)

The default setting for rs (number of bases in the restriction enzyme recognition seq is 4) and doesn't need much adjustment if using a standard datafile provided from DArT Ltd right?

Kind regards,
 Florian

messages.author: a3ea45e87285d820
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] gl.filter.hamming removes information from gl@other$loc.metrics (rdepth missing)
parts:
Hi Florian,

The default for rs is set to be appropriate for the restriction enzymes used by DArT with their usual selection of cutters PstI (recognition sequence 5'-CTGCA|
G-3') and SphI (5'-GCATG|C-3'). Setting a threshold of 0.25 means 4 bases out of 100 as you say.

All the best,

A
